answer.exemplar: A plan nobody has run is a guess: the steps may name the wrong artefact, the wrong command, or credentials the night operator does not have, and none of that shows until the pressure is on. The test that makes it real is a timed drill on a copy of production, following the steps end to end and recording how long the rollback actually took, which is what tells the team whether it is safe to start.

questions.explanation: Untested plans fail on the small details nobody checks when nobody has tried them, and a live incident is the worst possible moment to discover a wrong path or a missing permission. A rehearsal converts the document into a procedure with a known duration, and that measured duration is what lets anyone decide whether rolling back is even the right call under pressure.
questions.hint: Ask what the plan looks like the first time somebody actually follows it.

questions.stem: Trace this drill script and report the version it selects and how many newer versions it skips. rates <- [1, 2, 14, 22, 9]. names <- [v1, v2, v3, v4, v5]. limit <- 5. pick <- v1. FOR EACH i FROM 1 TO 5 { IF rates[i] <= limit { pick <- names[i] } } skipped <- 0. FOR EACH i FROM 1 TO 5 { IF rates[i] > limit { skipped <- skipped + 1 } } DISPLAY pick, skipped.
